# Synthetic Phase 0 fixtures — generated by running the real harness

The [frozen legacy bundles](../legacy/README.md) only ever exercised one path: report →
fixed. Duplicates and reopens did happen (28 and 10, per `../legacy/transitions-observed.tsv`)
but the mutable ledger overwrites the evidence, and escalation was never exercised at all. So
every remaining Phase 0 case is produced here.

**These are generated, not written.** [`generate.sh`](generate.sh) drives the actual
[`ledger.sh`](../../../../.agents/skills/self-review-heavy/scripts/ledger.sh) and
[`checks.sh`](../../../../.agents/skills/self-review-heavy/scripts/checks.sh) and records what
they really do. The harness is the specification the kernel must reproduce; a hand-authored
JSONL fixture would encode our reading of it instead of its behavior, and the reading is
exactly what a port gets wrong.

```sh
tools/review-kernel/fixtures/synthetic/generate.sh           # rewrite the corpus
tools/review-kernel/fixtures/synthetic/generate.sh --check   # prove it still reproduces
```

Every case asserts what it claims to prove, so `generate.sh` fails loudly if the harness ever
drifts from the corpus. `--check` regenerates into a temp directory and diffs — it passes
today, byte for byte.

## What a case contains

```text
<case>/
  CASE.md         what this case pins, and why the kernel must preserve it
  input/          the reviewer findings JSON (or check list) fed to the harness
  transcript.txt  every command, its stdout, its stderr, its exit code
  ledger.jsonl    the resulting ledger        (ledger.sh cases)
  round           the round counter           (ledger.sh cases)
  checks.tsv      the machine-readable result (checks.sh cases)
```

The **transcript is the fixture**. Exit codes and stderr are part of it: `converged` returns
three distinct verdicts (0 converged, 1 not yet, 3 exhausted), and the re-triage warning for a
re-reported rejection exists *only* on stderr — a kernel port that models stdout alone silently
drops it. `MANIFEST.tsv` indexes the corpus.

Two normalizations, both so the corpus is byte-reproducible, neither touching anything the
kernel's contracts depend on:

- the elapsed-seconds column in `checks.tsv` is rewritten to `<secs>`;
- an empty `checks/` directory gets a `.gitkeep`. `checks.sh` creates its log directory before it
  knows whether any check will run, so the vacuous case leaves it empty — and git cannot store an
  empty directory. Without the marker the directory survives locally and vanishes on clone, so
  `--check` passes only on the machine that generated the corpus. CI caught exactly that on its
  first run.

## Phase 0 coverage, completed

| Case | Pins |
|---|---|
| `duplicate-same-round` | one entry, first reporter wins, the second report is discarded entirely |
| `duplicate-later-round` | same-severity re-report bumps `last_seen_round` only — not news |
| `escalation` | higher severity adopts rank/evidence/source in place and **is** news |
| `reopen-after-fix` | a fix that did not hold reopens — and the resolution note is overwritten |
| `rejected-re-report-same-severity` | rejected never auto-reopens; the only signal is on stderr |
| `rejected-re-report-higher-severity` | rank adopted in place, status untouched, still news |
| `wontfix-re-report` | the wontfix branch behaves as rejected does |
| `contested-escalation` | contested blocks convergence and can escalate |
| `fix-needs-a-clean-round` | apply-without-confirmation: a same-round fix does not converge |
| `max-rounds-exhausted` | exit 3 is a third verdict, never a pass |
| `sub-gate-minor-never-blocks` | an open sub-gate finding converges anyway |
| `malformed-severity-rejected` | out-of-enum severity is refused before ingestion, exit 2 |
| `empty-title-skipped-batch-survives` | one bad finding cannot discard a valid batch; change-wide default |
| `check-vacuous-run-is-not-a-pass` | zero executed checks exits 1 — a missing check is not a pass |
| `check-failure-is-recorded` | a failure is recorded with its log and fails the run |
| `check-with-no-command-fails-the-run` | a malformed check line cannot quietly shrink the gate |

Two of these are worth reading before writing any kernel code, because they are the reason the
design has an append-only event log at all:

- `duplicate-same-round` — a second reviewer's independent report leaves **no trace**. The
  kernel keeps every report immutable and treats the fingerprint as a grouping hint.
- `reopen-after-fix` — the reopen note overwrites the resolution note, so afterwards the ledger
  cannot say what the fix claimed. A projection can be rebuilt; overwritten history cannot.

The adversarial cases the design also demands — late receipt, malicious check, hostile Git
config, cross-slice interaction — have no legacy equivalent to capture and are specified in
[`../adversarial/`](../adversarial/README.md) instead.
